summary: Regression test after Hero refactor (scroll-scrub removed, video now loops with timeupdate-driven cues, CTA always visible). All 24/24 frontend assertions passed on desktop (1920x1080) and mobile (390x844).

issues: During the 600ms cue cross-fade, two cue headlines can briefly visually overlap on small screens because .cue-active uses position:relative while the outgoing .cue-past keeps position:absolute. Functionally fine (only one cue is active at a time and CTA stays anchored), but a short stacking flicker is visible mid-transition. Consider tightening the transition timing on mobile or fading via a single shared positioned slot. NOT a regression — pre-existing transition behavior.

critical_code_review_comments: Hero useEffect correctly cleans up timeupdate listener on unmount; play() promise rejection is swallowed safely.
getCueIndex thresholds (0.15/0.45/0.7/0.92) are well distributed across the 5.04s loop — cue cycling validated empirically (samples observed cues 1,2,3,4,5).
reducedMotion branch sets activeCue=4 and pauses video (cue 5 'She's not real.' frozen). Confirmed not triggered in default tests.
Hero is now 100vh exactly (1080/1080 desktop, 844/844 mobile) — confirmed scroll past hero is natural (scrollY=200 after scrollTo(0,200)).
Hero CTA button extracted from cue 5 and confirmed always-visible across all 5 cues during 6+ seconds of observation.
No console errors detected on either viewport.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hero loop-mode regression confirmed green. All previous iteration_1 assertions still hold (sections, nav, stats=4, steps=3, who=5, final CTA mailto). Only minor cosmetic note is brief cue cross-fade overlap on mobile — not a regression and user explicitly approved the loop behavior. No further action needed.
